links.outcome: Whether LLM-only error classification suffices versus human-in-the-loop review
links.effect: Benchmarking six LLMs showed automated error classification alone is insufficient without human involvement.
links.quote: First, benchmarking of six proprietary and open-source LLMs shows that automated error classification alone is insufficient without human involvement.

links.outcome: Agreement with expert-adjudicated annotations and annotation time
links.effect: Agreement improved by up to 30% (McNemar exact test, p = 0.035, φ = 0.38) and annotation time decreased 26-33%.
links.quote: Third, prospective external validation at two independent institutions demonstrates improved agreement with expert-adjudicated annotations by up to 30% (McNemar exact test, p = 0.035, φ = 0.38) and reduced annotation time by 26-33%, providing a systematic and practical framework for real-world clinical NLP deployment.

links.effect: MedError-derived feedback improved performance by 34-62% over an unstructured baseline across 11 cognitive status concepts.
links.quote: Second, MedError-derived error feedback improves NLP extraction performance by 34-62% over an unstructured baseline across 11 cognitive status concepts.
